dedupe_keys.name: smartwater bgi planer blue green infrastructure planner for berlin

description: The BGI Planner is a map-based web application that helps staff in Berlin's planning departments, at Senate and district level, build blue-green infrastructure measures into new and existing planning processes so the city copes better with heavy rainfall and heat. Technologiestiftung Berlin develops it in the Smart Water project, part of the state's digital strategy, and the launch was reported in September 2026 as an open source tool for climate adaptation planning. It supports strategic choices in early planning and guidance for concrete measures later. The application is written in Next.js and TypeScript with OpenLayers maps and is deployed with Docker. Coverage is the City of Berlin. Format and access: an open source repository and a web application for city staff. Licence: MIT (Technologiestiftung Berlin, 2025); free. Caveats: it is designed for Berlin's administration and its data, and the page read does not describe the simulation models behind it. It supports climate adaptation planning of green-blue infrastructure. Related catalogue records are the Berlin Biotope Area Factor and Berlin's public green spaces data.
